findings.title: buyArtworks: "Platform cost" next to "Price" reads as an extra charge, but it is part of the price.

findings.title: buyArtworks: the "Pay via vault" raw true/false hides that true means the signer is not the payer.

findings.title: buyArtworks: payable with no @.value field; when paying through the vault, the ETH sent is unchecked and never shown.
findings.reason: When payByVaultContract is true, the vault pays the price, and nothing checks or refunds msg.value. Any ETH the buyer sends stays in the exhibition contract, which has no withdraw function, and the descriptor has no @.value field. The 'Pay via vault' and 'Price' fields do not show the ETH that leaves the wallet; test case 6 only covers the non-vault branch, where msg.value must equal the price.
findings.quote: FeralfileExhibitionV4_1.buyArtworks: `saleData_.payByVaultContract ? vault.payForSale(r_, s_, v_, saleData_) : require(saleData_.price == msg.value, "FeralfileExhibitionV4: invalid payment amount");` then `payable(costReceiver).transfer(leftOver)` with `leftOver = saleData_.price - distributedRevenue`. Descriptor buyArtworks fields: price, cost, destination, tokenIds, expiryTime, payByVaultContract, revenueShares; no `@.value`.

findings.title: startSale: the intent does not say it permanently ends minting for the owner and trustees.
findings.reason: Ending minting is what starting the sale means in this contract: resumeSale and pauseSale both require !mintable, so a sale cannot exist while minting is on. Not-critical case 12 covers this (a side effect that is the prerequisite or meaning of the stated action). No asset, allowance or position of the owner who signs moves, so it is at most a warning about the intent wording.
